{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table delivered a clear fish, a big outline with a back line, belly line and flared tail. By my check, the whole run was connected to the start and fell as one. My contribution was verification. I inspected the run five times during the build, covering the back line, the nose join and the doubled-up patch in the middle. Each time I confirmed the chain was connected, so the team could stop worrying about breaks and keep their hands off. I did not lay dominoes or draw the design, and I won't claim that.

Execution: I worked quietly and methodically. I used my inspection time on the spots where a fish run is most likely to fail: the joins and the crowded middle patch. I reported what I found clearly, including that nothing needed patching. When Hana was already laying the lower tail stroke, I stayed off it so our hands didn't collide or bump each other's dominoes. After the checks, I kept my hands off the table until the push, which protected the finished picture.

Collaboration: I offered to take a share of the belly and the lower tail, and when Hana had it covered I switched to checking the middle section she asked me to look at. I posted short, accurate updates to the whole table so everyone shared the same picture of the run's state. I followed the agreed rule of no extra handling in the final minutes.

Leadership: My leadership was modest. I kept the mood light, backed the fish plan early, and set a good example by stepping back when the work was covered. I supported the team's calls rather than competing with them. I'd like to take on more of the building and design in future rounds.", "my_share_percent": 10}
